data.narrative:
Tempo is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Nima Rahmatian, Kelvin Randhir, Joerg Petrasch, and Alessandro Bo, having raised $50M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of nine peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including one public company (Linz, LNZA) and eight private firms such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable data within the narrow peer set; no three or more directly comparable Series A or near-stage transactions were available despite eight same-sector peers existing broadly. Consequently, the valuation relies on stage-progression methodology, applying a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A advancement to the $50M raised proxy, yielding a midpoint of $100M.

The triangulated analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a range of $85M to $115M, with a median of $100M. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x step-up multiplier absent validated peer transaction data, and the absence of comparable-company validation at this stage. A fuller valuation would require either identification of additional same-stage private transactions or public comps with disclosed Series A entry multiples. This range should be treated as preliminary pending deeper market discovery.
